Reference sources and coverage

The reference pages bring together the game’s information, the hack author’s notes and recorded gameplay checks. When sources disagree or a route is uncertain, the relevant page explains what that means for your playthrough. This page keeps the detailed source accounting for anyone who wants to check it.

All 8,074 nonempty data/note rows from the three supplied workbooks are accounted for. Headers and blank rows are excluded. A row can have matching numeric fields and an unresolved effect, cost, location or source claim.

  • Game data Means a table, script or documented code/configuration comparison. It does not mean a completed battle or capture test.
  • Game description Means the translated description as written in the hack. Original descriptions, including stale wording, are retained in the records below.
  • Author note Means the author's claim. The item survey is labeled 3.2 and has several outdated locations and costs; older claims and comparisons are retained below.
  • Tested in game Is used only for existing documented gameplay tests, such as the calendar tests. The reference reconciliation added no new gameplay test.

The game data on these pages was read from the ROM that the v1.0.0-rc8 patch produces (SHA-1 a54a647599d59ed0060dfc4375c289d6e041318a), so it includes every fix that release turns on.

Workbook coverage

“Included” means the compared fields match or the claim has been included with attribution. It is not a blanket human-review verdict. “Unresolved” means a comparison or locator remains open. 21 included rows are reserved unnamed item slots with no useful gameplay note; their explicit disposition remains in the source register.

Species comparisons keep forms and genders distinct and compare the supplied evolution constraints with configured incoming or outgoing evolution edges. Encounter comparisons use the map header's table and exact species/form slots or method sets. Author numeric values and names do not replace game records.

Remaining reference limitations

  • Some EN-workbook Pokémon and encounter names differ from both the configured data and the earlier translated Chinese survey. These are source conflicts; they are not automatically new hack bugs.
  • Move and ability special effects have not all been decoded or tested. Applicability flags are configuration evidence. The 13 Mega Launcher interactions remain author claims; the 23 author-listed Sharpness moves all have the slicing flag, alongside nine other configured slicing moves.
  • Item rarity and repeatability labels remain author claims. The separately labeled original-game source column can mention older or unavailable facilities. Player pages show usable acquisition instructions; the underlying comparisons remain below.
  • Tutor payment data does not establish every story prerequisite. Author access comparisons remain below. Unknown cost data is shown as unknown; only an explicitly empty configured cost list is shown as free.
  • Stored trainer parties and scripted appearances are linked. No earlier party is invented as a comparison baseline, and unmapped teams remain availability-unconfirmed.
  • Five source land tables contain 180 rows without a map reference. Their species entries are retained below without inventing an in-game location, level or rate. The Map Overview label “Sootopolis Sea” also has no supported area mapping.

Author trade-goods note

Author note The author lists Pearl, Big Pearl, Nugget, Rare Bone, Stardust and Star Piece as exchange goods. The EN attachment instead names Big Root where the translated Chinese survey names Rare Bone; use the configured exchanges on item pages.

Author map locator and standalone notes

The source's numeric locators and labels can disagree. They are preserved here as author notes, separately from the location catalog and TM shop records.

Location uncertain: the reference gives conflicting place names. See the source details before following it.

Detailed reference records

Gameplay pages use concise summaries. These records preserve the original descriptions, author wording, comparison results, raw fields and existing test limits. No new gameplay testing is implied.

Moves

Move stat comparisons use the untouched Pokémon HeartGold (USA) table, normalized in work/tools/site/move_original_facts.json. Only original moves 1–467 have that baseline; dummy and trailing records are excluded. For later moves, an advertised change may give only its new value. Effect changes use the separate author notes, live fields and existing gameplay reports; the original and hack effect IDs are never treated as interchangeable meanings. Dragon Claw’s advertised critical-hit boost is not confirmed: its live effect and critical-hit fields retain the original values.

Blast Burn

Original in-game description: The foe is razed by a fierce, fiery explosion. It has a 10% chance to burn the target.

In the recorded Lv. 100 user versus wild Pokémon scenario, the command menu returned after one Blissey attack following Blast Burn, versus two after Hyper Beam. No recharge turn occurred in that scenario. Frenzy Plant, Hydro Cannon and Rock Wrecker were not tested.

Recharge in other situations is not confirmed.

guide/known-issues.md, Moves that work differently; D-1318; emu_harness.py hackbugs --case move; both ROMs

Bounce

Original in-game description: The user bounces up and drops on the foe in a single turn. 30% chance to paralyze the foe.

In the recorded probe, Bounce attacked on the selected turn: no spring-up message or miss appeared, and the command menu returned every turn. Fly took two turns as a control. This is a scoped result, not verification of every effect field.

Other effects and battle situations are not confirmed.

Volt Tackle

Original in-game description: The user unleashes a high-voltage shock. It may leave the foe paralyzed.

In the recorded KO scenario, a Lv. 100 user defeated a wild Magikarp with Volt Tackle and lost no HP; Double-Edge cost 4 HP as a control. This does not establish recoil behavior in other scenarios.

Recoil in other situations is not confirmed.

Lunar Dance

Original in-game description: The user dances in the moonlight. Raises its Sp. Atk and Speed by 1 stage.

In the recorded Lv. 100 user versus wild Pokémon scenario, Lunar Dance raised the user's Speed and Sp. Atk and the user remained in battle. Other conditions and special-effect behavior remain unverified.

Other effects and battle situations are not confirmed.

---
title: Mechanics and controls
description: EXP sharing, capture chains, EV training, evolution rules, held-item forms and the controls added in Origin HeartGold v4.0.3.
---

import FormChanges from '../../components/FormChanges.astro';
import { formChanges } from '../../lib/verified-mechanics';

Origin HeartGold changes more than the story. These notes describe **v4.0.3**, checked against the original Chinese game's code. The EXP/EV award example and information-screen controls were also checked in the emulator. Where a full gameplay test is still missing, the limits are stated below.

## Information-screen controls

These are **Nintendo DS buttons**, not particular keyboard keys. Use the corresponding buttons in your emulator or on your controller.

| Where | Button | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Pokémon summary, stats/moves page | **L** | Show IVs and EVs together |
| IV/EV panel | **L or B** | Close the panel |
| Battle command menu | **Y**, or tap the information button at the top right of the touch screen | Open battle information |
| Battle-information panel | **B** | Close the panel |

If the first Y press only highlights a battle command, press Y again. The panel shows information such as stat stages and your Pokémon's ability; it is not a promise that an opponent's unrevealed ability will be visible.

The summary shortcut was tested with normal button settings. **R did not open the IV/EV panel** in that mode, despite the game's L/R hint.

## Automatic EXP and EV sharing

Your party shares battle **experience points (EXP)** and **effort values (EVs)** automatically. EVs are training points that affect a Pokémon's stats; IVs are its individual stat values.

In a controlled battle, the participating Pokémon received **26 EXP**, the benched Pokémon **13 EXP**, and both gained **1 HP EV**. This illustrates the nonparticipant half-EXP path, not a promise that every battle gives those amounts. Eggs, fainted party members and every special battle mode were not tested.

There is **no native on/off setting for this sharing** in the inspected v4.0.3 battle code. You do not need the held Exp. Share to enable it. Keep party-wide EV gains in mind when training.

## Capture chains

The [Chain Logger](../items/chain-logger/) is added to your Bag during new-game setup. Use it to inspect your chain and the area's encounters.

Catching the same **species and form** builds a chain. The bonuses use the number already caught before the next encounter is generated:

| Completed catches | Hidden Ability selection chance from the chain | Distinct IVs forced to 31 |
|---|---:|---:|
| 0–5 | No chain bonus | 0 |
| 6–9 | 10% | 1 |
| 10–19 | 50% | 2 |
| 20+ | 70% | 4 |

A Pokémon may naturally have more perfect IVs. Hidden Ability selection still depends on that species' ability data.

**The game's displayed ranges are inaccurate around 10 and 20.** The verified boundaries are 6, 10 and 20 catches. Shiny chances also improve, but the displayed fractions do not establish the exact combined probability; they should not be used as precise odds.

- Catching a different species **or form** starts a new chain at **1**.
- Catching a shiny of the **same species and form** clears the chain.
- A shiny of a **different species or form** follows the new-chain rule and starts at **1**.
- Defeating or fleeing does not advance the chain; no reset on those actions was found in the inspected handlers.

The bonuses can apply to a different species from the one you chained, including the traced scripted wild encounters. Gifts, Eggs and every special encounter are not covered by that verification. The chain counter stops increasing at 255.

## EV Allocator

The [EV Allocator](../items/ev-allocator/) is added after battle if you do not already have one. This is verified in the battle-end code; the exact first acquisition screen has not been replayed.

It **redistributes EVs you already earned**. It does not create new training points. Before exiting, you must restore each party member's total to the amount it had when you opened the tool.

| Button | Action |
|---|---|
| Left / Right | Decrease / increase the selected EV by 4 |
| L / R | Decrease / increase it by 64 |
| X / Y | Previous / next party member |
| SELECT | Open the clear-EVs confirmation |
| START | Open the restore-entry-EVs confirmation |

These allocator mappings were read from the normal-button-mode handler; all confirmation and alternative-button-mode combinations have not been played through.

## Mom's charms

Mom's savings purchases include these three charms. Each purchase is queued for delivery and deducts money from your savings; reaching a threshold does not mean immediate receipt.

| Charm | Savings threshold | Cost from savings |
|---|---:|---:|
| [Catching Charm](../items/catching-charm/) | $30,000 | $3,000 |
| [Exp. Charm](../items/exp-charm/) | $40,000 | $3,000 |
| [Shiny Charm](../items/shiny-charm/) | $50,000 | $3,000 |

**There is no Oval Charm** in this game: nothing gives it, and no code checks for it.

## Visible encounters and shinies

The game supports up to **six visible wild Pokémon** nearby. Repel suppresses new visible spawns; immediate removal of existing spawns was not verified. Ordinary encounter frequency is reduced in some conditions while visible Pokémon are present, but it is not an unconditional one-third rate everywhere.

A visible shiny has a sparkle and sound cue. The game keeps **one temporary shiny record** and can use it when you re-enter the same map, searching for a position near you. Terrain can still prevent an accessible placement, and another shiny can replace the single record.

**Catch a visible shiny before restarting.** The retained record is cleared during game boot. Do not rely on an ordinary save to preserve it: save/load restoration has not been established. Emulator save states are a separate mechanism.

Special [calendar encounters](../calendar/) modify particular land encounters on annual dates. They are listed separately from the ordinary location tables.

## Evolution

The hack rewrites many evolutions. Each [Pokémon](../pokemon/) page lists how it evolves, read from the game code, and what changed from HeartGold. The main rules:

- **No trading needed for the old trade evolutions.** Kadabra, Machoke, Graveler, Haunter and the rest now evolve when they level up holding an item, often only by day or by night (for example Haunter → Gengar holding a Spell Tag at night, Machoke → Machamp holding a Black Belt by day). Onix and Porygon simply level up.
- **Day and night:** night is 20:00–3:59, "day" is 4:00–19:59. A few evolutions need 10:00–16:59 and say so.
- **Friendship:** "high friendship" means 220 or more; Sylveon needs 158 or more plus a Fairy-type move.
- **The first match wins:** Meowth, Slowpoke and Cubone must take their held-item evolution before the level of their normal one, and Eevee checks Sylveon and Espeon before Glaceon.
- **Some evolutions can't happen:** a few methods in the data are never checked by the game. Most belong to Pokémon that can't be met anyway; the ones that matter are Moss Rock Leafeon and magnetic-field Probopass, which still evolve with a Leaf Stone or Thunder Stone. See [Known issues](../guide/known-issues/#evolutions-that-cannot-happen).

## Held-item forms

<FormChanges entries={formChanges} />

Use the [move reference](../moves/) for stats, effects and learning methods, and the [ability reference](../abilities/) to find abilities for your team. The [TM/HM list](../tms/) shows where to get each machine and which Pokémon can use it.

## Other training and battle changes

- **Pickup:** successful Pickup deposits go straight into the Bag. An empty held-item slot is not required by the inspected routine. Full-Bag behavior was not tested.
- **Held items after battle:** the game restores many items, but has exceptions, including special berry handling. Do not assume every consumed, stolen or knocked-off item comes back.
- **Hatching:** both Flame Body and Magma Armor enable an eight-cycle decrement. Small remaining counters decrease more slowly, so this is not exactly eight times fewer steps for every Egg. Multiple holders do not stack in this routine.
- **Destiny Knot:** either parent holding it raises inherited IV slots to five. This does not guarantee five perfect IVs.
- **Everstone:** a single holder supports nature inheritance, but the two-holder and different-language breeding paths prevent a blanket guarantee. Those exceptions have not been tested with a full Egg-hatching series.

## Field moves

The hack intentionally lets you use scripted obstacle moves without teaching them to a Pokémon. Badge requirements still apply, and party-menu moves have separate restrictions. See the [field-move table](../guide/ch01-first-badge/#field-moves-which-badge-each-one-needs) for the precise distinctions.


---
title: Calendar encounters
description: Annual date-specific land encounters configured in Origin HeartGold v4.0.3, with availability caveats.
---

import CalendarEncounters from '../../components/CalendarEncounters.astro';
import { calendarEncounters } from '../../lib/verified-mechanics';

The game changes a land encounter slot in certain places on these **annual dates**, using the game's calendar. Every entry below was tested in an emulator, on the Chinese original and on the English patch: on the date the area's encounter table had the entry in its last land slot, and the day before it didn't. With that slot forced (so the test didn't wait for the 1% roll), each Pokémon appeared at the level shown and was caught with a Master Ball. How the entries combine with other encounter modifiers (abilities, Swarms, the radio) wasn't tested.

They replace the final land slot, normally weighted **1% of land encounters**, while keeping its existing level. That is not a 1% chance per step. In the emulator test, with that slot forced, the Pokémon walking around in the grass were the calendar Pokémon too, so it can probably also show up as one of them; how often wasn't measured. They do not replace Surf or fishing slots.

**The game reads the date when you enter the area.** If the date changes while you are already there (for example at midnight), you still meet the old day's Pokémon, also after a battle: leave the area and come back. Tested in an emulator.

**Morning:** 04:00–09:59. **Day:** 10:00–19:59. **Night:** 20:00–03:59. The month and day must still match: July 18's night window does not extend into July 19. These windows were checked in an emulator at Mt. Silver on July 18 (03:59, 04:00, 09:59, 10:00, 19:59 and 20:00).

<CalendarEncounters entries={calendarEncounters} />

The [ordinary encounter tables](../locations/) and [source comparisons](../reference-sources/) are separate references. A matching author encounter row does not extend the calendar tests to every encounter modifier.

## Entries that need care

**Diancie:** the entry uses a form number the game doesn't define, so the game falls back to the normal form: you meet a normal Diancie, not Mega Diancie. Tested in an emulator: the Diancie you meet and catch has the normal sprite, Rock/Fairy type and a normal Diancie's stats.

**Volcanion:** the game also configures an April 16 entry at Lake of Rage, but Lake of Rage has no grass and no land encounters, so it never appears. In an emulator, walking around Lake of Rage on April 16 (morning, day and night, with the slot forced) gave no encounter at all, and no event script, trade or other encounter table in the game gives Volcanion. It can't be met in this version, so it isn't listed.

These entries are separate from the [Wednesday Lake of Rage events](../guide/ch30-hq-round-4/#lake-of-rage-when-the-calm-day-happens-continues-lake-of-rage-blackthorn-city-and-beyonds-lake-trio-and-calm-day-visitors) and from [visible encounters and shiny retention](../mechanics/#visible-encounters-and-shinies).

Calendar and held-item form research

Calendar encounters
[
  {
